oil.summary: Crude suffered a sharp sell-off on 4 August, with WTI shedding 4.4% to $76.81 and Brent falling 3.8% to $80.56, even as the geopolitical backdrop remains highly charged. The apparent contradiction lies in supply-side relief signals: the US reportedly eased Russia oil sanctions on a temporary basis to tame the recent price surge, and Iran-Oman talks on the Strait of Hormuz are said to be nearing completion, raising hopes of restored Gulf export flows. Those developments appear to be outweighing bullish headlines — Ukrainian drone strikes hitting multiple Russian refineries and a strategic airbase, and Iran's stated intent to maintain its oil blockade until attacks cease. RBOB gasoline's extraordinary 12% single-day plunge amplifies demand-side concern. Options markets assign a 77% probability to an OPEC cut at the next meeting, signalling that the producer group may view current prices as uncomfortably low.
drivers: US temporary easing of Russia oil sanctions and progress on Iran-Oman Hormuz talks inject near-term supply-relief sentiment, pressuring prices
RBOB gasoline collapsed 12% on the day and 22% on the week, pointing to significant demand-side weakness or a crack-spread unwind
Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and Iran's continued oil blockade threat provide an unresolved geopolitical risk floor, limiting the downside conviction

gas.summary: Henry Hub eased 3.9% on the day to $2.671/MMBtu, though it remains marginally positive on the week, suggesting today's move may be profit-taking after recent stability rather than a fundamental shift. The month-on-month decline of nearly 18% underscores persistent domestic oversupply pressure. European TTF shed 2.4% to €56.14/MWh but remains up 27% on the month, reflecting a very different supply tightness dynamic in Europe — likely linked to the broader geopolitical disruptions visible in the oil sector. No sector-specific gas headlines were available in today's feed; the price moves are noted but cannot be attributed to specific catalysts beyond the macro context.
drivers: Henry Hub down 3.9% on the day, extending a steep 18% monthly decline consistent with ongoing US supply surplus
TTF holds a 27% monthly gain despite today's softness, reflecting Europe's tighter supply environment tied to geopolitical disruption
No gas-specific news flow available today; price moves interpreted in macro context only

power.summary: EU carbon allowances (EUA) bucked the broader energy sell-off, edging up 0.8% to $77.61, though the weekly and monthly moves remain modest at -0.5% and +1.7% respectively, suggesting rangebound price discovery. The power and carbon sector had limited dedicated headline flow today; the two relevant items concern Iran policy signals — Trump's mixed messages on winding down the Iran conflict and Iran-Oman Strait of Hormuz talks nearing completion. Both are primarily oil-market narratives with indirect implications for European energy costs and carbon pricing. TTF's continued elevation (up 27% on the month) sustains gas-to-coal switching incentives and supports carbon demand at the margin, which may explain EUA's mild outperformance relative to other energy assets today.
drivers: EUA edged up 0.8%, modestly outperforming a broadly weaker energy complex, likely supported by elevated TTF keeping gas-fired generation competitive and carbon demand firm
TTF's 27% monthly surge sustains the structural case for carbon demand, even as today's 2.4% daily dip provides marginal relief to power generators
Dedicated power and carbon headline flow is thin today; Iran-Hormuz developments are the primary macro variable to monitor for European energy cost pass-through
